claims: Weeknight work after 10.00 pm is ${$(2.95)} an hour extra until midnight and ${$(4.42)} an hour extra after midnight.
whys: The two flat amounts are typed into the page copy as literals, not read from the award data. They match the constants today, but the 1 July rate update will not reach this sentence. The constants set them as 10% and 15% of the Level 4 standard hourly rate, so they change every year.
reviewerNotes: The restaurant weeknight flat amounts $(2.95) and $(4.42) are typed as literals instead of being read from MODERN_AWARDS.restaurant penalties[].flatPerHour (lib/constants/modern-awards.ts lines 1010-1011). The writer's factQuestion is valid.

whys: I checked these figures against 2026-27 rates and they are correct now. But they are hard-coded in the FAQ, while the page body works out the same figures with netPay(). They will be wrong after the next tax change. Line 21 also hard-codes 47% where the page uses NO_TFN_RATES.resident.

claims: Use your existing fund, or switch to the employer's default if it has lower fees.
In most cases, use your existing fund ... If the employer's default fund has significantly lower fees, it may be worth switching.
whys: The answer leaves out super stapling (in force since 1 November 2021). If a new employee makes no choice, the employer must ask the ATO for the employee's stapled fund before it can use its default fund. So the either/or framing is incomplete.

'In most cases' is a population or advice claim with no source. Recommending a super fund also sits close to financial product advice. The answer should be checked together with the stapling gap the writer flagged.
constants: lib/constants (super choice and stapling rule, ATO source)

claims: On your TFN Declaration, tick "Yes" if you have a HELP, VSL, SFSS, or TSL debt.
whys: The current ATO TFN declaration lists HELP, VSL, FS (Financial Supplement), SSL (Student Start-up Loan) and TSL. 'SFSS' is the old name, and SSL is missing from the list.
constants: HECS_HELP in lib/constants (study-loan list for the TFN declaration)

claims: The only difference during probation is that the notice period for termination is typically shorter (usually 1 week).
whys: The NES notice period depends on length of service (1 week under 1 year), not on probation. The main legal effect of probation is the unfair dismissal minimum employment period (6 months, or 12 months for a small business). 'The only difference' looks wrong.
constants: lib/constants (NES notice periods and unfair dismissal minimum employment period, FWO source)
